summary: Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post as a research assistant at Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professorship at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2012).
Hiroyuki Kato was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held positions at Bansho Shirabesho (c. 1860–1862), the Kaisei School (c. 1863–1868), and the University of Tokyo (c. 1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University from around 1926 to 1929. He later held a post at Kyoto Sangyo University from approximately 1969 to 1983.

Hisao Inagaki specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and SOAS University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at Doshisha University (c. 1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (c. 1950–1963) and Komazawa University (c. 1982–1989), and honorary professor at Tokyo Metropolitan University (c. 1963–1982).

Hisao Takahashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He spent his career at Taisho University as an assistant (c. 1974–1982), lecturer (c. 1989–1996), and professor (c. 1996–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and later served as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato, a scholar of Tibetology and history, studied at Kyoto University (c. 1933–1936). He was later a professor at Kyoto University (c. 1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and also held a post at Bukkyo University (c. 1977–1984).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, later serving as a full-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Hisatake Kato was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1957–1967). He held academic posts at Yamagata University, the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and the University of Human Arts and Sciences.

Hisayoshi Miyamoto is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He has held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He has served at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1992 he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University, and he later held an affiliation at Osaka University (attested 2016).

Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and earned a doctorate from SOAS University of London. He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS starting in 1948 and became Professor of Burmese (1966–1980).

Ho-chin Yang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Yang completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, graduating in 1994.
Hogen Bays is a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. He has served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a disciple under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1953. He later completed studies at Ryukoku University from approximately 1959 to 1963.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (c. 1999–2003) and KU Leuven (c. 2005–2007), and who also taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar with a doctorate in literature. Affiliations (attested 2026) include positions at Minobusan University, the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, Doho University, and Daido University Graduate School.
